public_rationale: OpenAI's December 9, 2024 launch announcement said the deployed Sora version often generated unrealistic physics and struggled with complex actions over long durations [e1]. It also reported that Sora Turbo was significantly faster than the February preview [e1]. The acknowledged recurring physics failures support the claim that these problems had not been robustly solved by December 2024 [e1].
limitations: The evidence concerns the December 2024 release, not later versions.
It does not quantify changes in physics reliability or separately establish the frequency of object-continuity failures.
It establishes neither spending totals nor the causal effect of additional time or money.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Between February and December 2024, time and money did not robustly solve Sora's physics problems.

statement.excerpt: Time and money haven’t robustly solved these problems.
statement.document_title: Sora still appears to have trouble with physics

our_interpretation: The context compares the February preview with the December release, ending at the December 10 post.
The ordinary reading of 'robustly solved' is reliable handling of physical interactions and object continuity, rather than occasional successful outputs.
This is an observation about the result of development to date. It does not claim that progress was absent, identify a spending amount, or estimate the causal effect of additional spending.
Because no financial quantity is asserted, metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence about the December release establishes that physical inconsistencies or continuity failures remain recurring limitations after the development interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence about the December release establishes reliable handling of the relevant physical interactions and object continuity, with the earlier failure modes substantially resolved rather than remaining recurring limitations.
